clue.text: Wearside city is buried?

blocks.note: 'is' contracted to 's, as in it's
something buried is under land

explanation.surface: A quiz question asking whether a northern English city has been buried.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the playful reading: 'is buried' becomes 's under land'. Wearside is the area around the River Wear in north-east England.
explanation.definitionFit: Sunderland is the principal city on the River Wear, so it is the Wearside city by example.

clue.text: Reportedly look for religious adherent

indicators.note: what is reported is passed on by word of mouth, so the sound counts rather than the spelling

blocks.note: to look for something is to seek it

explanation.surface: A report says someone goes searching for a devout believer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'look for' reads as one phrase, but 'for' is the link and 'look' alone is the verb to seek.
explanation.definitionFit: A Sikh is a follower of Sikhism, the faith founded by Guru Nanak in the Punjab.

clue.text: No petrol spilled outside hot and cold location

indicators.note: spilled liquid splashes everywhere, so the letters end up scattered into a new order
to be outside something is to surround it, so one piece goes around another

blocks.note: the letters as printed, to be rearranged
H is the abbreviation for hot on taps

explanation.surface: A garage has run out of fuel, leaving a place that is both hot and cold.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hot and cold' reads as a single phrase, but 'hot' is the letter going inside and 'and' just joins it to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The Arctic's northernmost point is a famously freezing spot, an example of a frigid place on the globe.

clue.text: Bounder dying to tour Californian city

indicators.note: to tour a place is to travel all round it, so one piece goes around another

blocks.note: dying is coming to an end
LA is Los Angeles

explanation.surface: A cad on his deathbed wants one last trip round Los Angeles.
explanation.walkthrough: A bounder is old British slang for a cad, but here it is literally something that bounds.
explanation.definitionFit: The eland is a large African antelope that leaps well, so it is a jumping animal, a crossword-style sense.

clue.text: Light working bathes one's head in caricature

indicators.note: the head of a word is its front, so only the opening letter is kept
to bathe something is to surround it with water, so one piece wraps another

blocks.note: a lamp is a light
a machine that is working is on
the first letter of the word

explanation.surface: A working lamp shines on someone's head in a cartoon drawing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bathes' looks like light flooding a face, but it means one piece wraps another; 'one's head' is just the first letter of 'one'.
explanation.definitionFit: A lampoon is a satirical attack mocking someone, much as a caricature exaggerates features for ridicule.

clue.text: Writer returning very fine Scottish port

indicators.note: to return is to go back the way you came, so the letters run backwards

blocks.note: V is the abbreviation for very
OK means all right, fine
Oban is a port on Scotland's west coast

explanation.surface: An author heads back to a lovely Scottish harbour town.
explanation.walkthrough: Oban is a ferry port in western Scotland; in a down clue 'returning' sends the whole string upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Vladimir Nabokov was the Russian-American novelist who wrote Lolita and Pale Fire.

clue.text: Madam Weisberg's opening immoral houses?

indicators.note: an opening is where something starts, so just the first letter is kept
to house something is to hold it inside, so one piece sits within another

blocks.note: immoral means bad
the first letter of the name

explanation.surface: A brothel keeper called Madam Weisberg opens some disreputable establishments.
explanation.walkthrough: 'houses' looks like a noun for brothels, fitting the madam, but it is a verb meaning holds.
explanation.definitionFit: A madam runs a brothel, and a bawd is the old word for exactly such a woman.

clue.text: Gods above initially make progress to the north

indicators.note: initially means at the start, so only the first letter is kept
in a down clue going north means reading upwards, so the letters run backwards

blocks.note: first letter of the word
to rise is to get on, make progress

explanation.surface: Deities in the heavens first advance northwards.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Gods above' reads as one phrase, but 'above' is only the source of its initial letter.
explanation.definitionFit: The Aesir are the principal Norse pantheon, including Odin and Thor, so they are a group of deities.

clue.text: Theme park designated driver's insanely drunk inside

indicators.note: a drunk person staggers about out of order, so the letters are jumbled
inside means within, so one piece goes into another

blocks.note: the first letters of designated and driver, the standard initials for that role; the 's means 'has'
the letters as printed, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: At a theme park the person meant to drive home is wildly drunk.
explanation.walkthrough: 'insanely' looks like an adverb on 'drunk', but it is the raw material and 'drunk' is the signal to mix it.
explanation.definitionFit: Disneyland is the California amusement resort built by Walt Disney, the archetypal themed fun park.

clue.text: Spoiled plot enclosing land

indicators.note: to enclose is to fence in, so one piece surrounds another

blocks.note: a garden plot is a bed
to light on, or alight, is to land

explanation.surface: A ruined allotment surrounded by farmland.
explanation.walkthrough: 'land' looks like a noun but is the verb, as when a bird lights on a branch.
explanation.definitionFit: Something blighted has been ruined or damaged, as crops are by disease, matching the sense of ruined.

clue.text: Some dhansak? Or madras? Something milder?

indicators.note: some means a portion of the whole, so the answer is a run of letters inside the words

blocks.note: the letters run across the gap between the two curry names

explanation.surface: Ordering at an Indian restaurant: perhaps a dhansak, a madras, or something less spicy?
explanation.walkthrough: Dhansak and madras are both curries, so the solver hunts for a third; it is sitting across their join.
explanation.definitionFit: A korma is a creamy, gently spiced curry, far less fiery than a madras, so by example a gentler dish.

clue.text: Lawgiver hoarding metals prepares for war

indicators.note: to hoard is to keep things stored away inside, so one piece holds another

blocks.note: Moses brought the Ten Commandments down from Sinai
Bi is bismuth and Li is lithium, two metal symbols

explanation.surface: A legislator stockpiles metal as the nation readies for conflict.
explanation.walkthrough: 'metals' gives two chemical symbols side by side, bismuth then lithium, both placed inside the prophet.
explanation.definitionFit: To mobilise is to assemble troops and resources for active service, getting a country ready for fighting.

clue.text: Seconds served with fish and pomelo

indicators.note: food served with something is put beside it on the plate, so one piece sits next to another

blocks.note: S is the abbreviation for seconds
the haddock is a North Atlantic food fish

explanation.surface: A second helping of fish arrives alongside a citrus fruit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Seconds' looks like a second helping at dinner, but it is just the unit abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: The shaddock is an older name for the pomelo, the large thick-skinned citrus fruit, named after a ship's captain.

clue.text: Sharp spines on this: son bloodied as it were?

indicators.note: this phrase flags a figurative reading: something covered in blood is wrapped in it, so one piece sits inside another

blocks.note: S is the abbreviation for son
gore is spilt blood, so to be bloodied is to be in it

explanation.surface: A boy scratched and bleeding after tumbling into a prickly bush.
explanation.walkthrough: The son ends up inside the blood, which is the playful sense of being bloodied.
explanation.definitionFit: Gorse, also called furze or whin, is a yellow-flowered shrub covered in sharp thorns.

clue.text: Over days tribe consumes brown sausage variety

indicators.note: what is consumed is taken inside, so one piece goes within another
in a down clue over means placed above, so one piece comes before the next

blocks.note: a clan is a tribe
umber is a brown earth pigment
D is the abbreviation for days

explanation.surface: For days a tribe has been eating a kind of brown banger.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Over days' sounds like a span of time, but it is placement: the rest stands above D.
explanation.definitionFit: Cumberland sausage is a long coiled pork sausage from the old English county of Cumberland, one type of banger.

clue.text: Idealistic local one holding back seaworthy vessel

indicators.note: going back means running the other way, so the letters are reversed
to hold something is to grip it inside, so one piece surrounds another

blocks.note: 'un is dialect for one, as a local might say it
A1 means first class, originally a ship rating; the 1 is read as I
a pot is a vessel

explanation.surface: A dreamy local man restrains a boat fit to sail.
explanation.walkthrough: A1 comes from Lloyd's Register of ships, so it fairly stands for seaworthy; the digit doubles as the letter I.
explanation.definitionFit: Utopian describes visionary schemes for a perfect society, aiming at unrealistic perfection like the dreamer.

clue.text: Laid up in old island state

blocks.note: someone laid up is ill in bed
taken as written
O is the abbreviation for old
IS is the abbreviation for island

explanation.surface: Bedridden in an ancient island nation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' looks like a placement instruction but is simply two letters in the charade.
explanation.definitionFit: Illinois is a Midwestern US state whose largest city is Chicago.

clue.text: Extremely vocal about one group in bitter criticism

indicators.note: extremes are the far ends, so only the outer letters are kept
about means around, so one piece surrounds another

blocks.note: the first and last letters of the word
I is the Roman numeral for one
a trio is a group of three

explanation.surface: A singer's outspoken attack on a band's members.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Extremely vocal' reads as very loud, but it only takes the two ends of the word.
explanation.definitionFit: Vitriol, literally sulphuric acid, figuratively means caustic and savage verbal attack.

clue.text: Lover, a Catholic raised in Italian area

indicators.note: in a down clue raising means lifting upwards, so the letters read backwards
in means inside, so one piece sits within another

blocks.note: taken as written
a Roman Catholic is a Roman
IT is the abbreviation for Italian
A is the abbreviation for area

explanation.surface: A Catholic sweetheart grew up in a region of Italy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Italian area' looks like a single place, but it is two abbreviations, and the reversed piece goes inside the first.
explanation.definitionFit: An inamorata is a woman who is loved, a female sweetheart, from the Italian for being enamoured.

clue.text: Fabulous group caught certain insects

indicators.note: to catch a word is to hear it, so the sound is wanted rather than the spelling

blocks.note: the Fab Four, the Liverpool band

explanation.surface: A legendary band managed to net some bugs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fabulous' points at the Fab Four nickname for the Liverpool pop group, and 'caught' looks like trapping rather than hearing.
explanation.definitionFit: Beetles are the order of insects with hardened wing cases, so they are one particular kind of bug.

clue.text: Drink on tick for boss

blocks.note: to sup is to drink
re means on, concerning
a tick and a mo are both a moment

explanation.surface: Buying drinks on credit for the manager.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on tick' is British slang for on credit, but here 'on' and 'tick' are separate pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: A supremo is the person in overall charge of an organisation, a chief or head.

clue.text: Breath so taken when hotel hosts raffle

indicators.note: a host holds guests inside, so one piece contains another

blocks.note: an inn is a hotel
a raffle is a draw

explanation.surface: A collective gasp as the prize draw is held at a hotel.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is a descriptive phrase: breath taken in this way.
explanation.definitionFit: Breath that is inhaled sharply is described as drawn in, which is what the adjective means.

clue.text: Pushed home, spoke of having vision

indicators.note: what is spoken is heard rather than read, so a sound-alike spelling is wanted

blocks.note: being at home is being in
someone with vision is sighted

explanation.surface: Someone forced through a plan while describing their grand vision.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pushed home' reads as one phrase meaning pressed an advantage, but the definition is just the first word.
explanation.definitionFit: To incite someone is to urge or spur them on, which is to push them toward action.

clue.text: Bird needs dressing endlessly

indicators.note: without an end means the final letter is cut off

blocks.note: robing is putting on robes, dressing

explanation.surface: A bird requires constant bandaging or grooming.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dressing' suggests a wound dressing or salad dressing, but it is the act of putting on robes.
explanation.definitionFit: The robin is a small songbird with a red breast, familiar in gardens.

clue.text: Chuck lassoes very large animal

indicators.note: a lasso loops round its target, so one piece surrounds another

blocks.note: to chuck something out is to bin it
so means very, as in so good

explanation.surface: A cowboy named Chuck ropes a huge beast.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Chuck' looks like a cowboy's name, but it is the verb to throw away. 'very large' reads as one phrase; only 'very' is wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: The bison is a massive wild ox of North America and Europe, a big hoofed beast.

clue.text: Choose an ancient character, said witty sort

indicators.note: said means spoken out, so the sound matters rather than the spelling

blocks.note: to choose is to pick, and a rune is an old Germanic letter

explanation.surface: Instructions to select a letter from an old alphabet, given to a joker.
explanation.walkthrough: Runes were the characters of early Germanic alphabets; the whole phrase spoken quickly makes the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A picaroon is a rogue or adventurer, and by extension a roguish wag; Chambers lists the jesting sense.

clue.text: Cyclist free here in the middle

indicators.note: the middle of a word is its centre, so only the central letters are kept

blocks.note: to rid is to free of something
the two central letters of the word

explanation.surface: A cyclist rides freely here in the centre of town.
explanation.walkthrough: 'free' looks like an adjective but is the verb to rid.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone on a bicycle is said to ride it, so a cyclist is one who rides.

clue.text: One was Rosebud, burned in Bois-le-Duc

indicators.note: in means contained within, so the answer sits inside the printed letters

blocks.note: the letters run across the hyphen in the town name

explanation.surface: A film buff's line: Rosebud was burnt in a Dutch town.
explanation.walkthrough: In Citizen Kane, Rosebud is the childhood toboggan seen burning at the end. Bois-le-Duc is the French name for 's-Hertogenbosch in the Netherlands.
explanation.definitionFit: Kane's dying word Rosebud named the snow toboggan he rode as a boy, which goes into the furnace in the final scene.

clue.text: Sober sailors can at last see holy work

indicators.note: at last means at the very end, so only the final letter is kept

blocks.note: ABs are able seamen
a tin is a can
the final letter of the word
NT is the New Testament

explanation.surface: Teetotal sailors can finally witness religious work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'can' looks like a verb meaning are able, but it is the noun for a container.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone abstinent refrains from alcohol, so they are not drunk, matching the teetotal sense.

clue.text: Slow speech from medic, boring thing

blocks.note: DR is the abbreviation for doctor
an awl is a tool for boring holes

explanation.surface: A doctor delivers a dull, ponderous lecture.
explanation.walkthrough: 'boring thing' suggests something tedious, but it is a tool that bores holes.
explanation.definitionFit: A drawl is a lazy manner of talking with drawn-out vowels.

clue.text: Scandinavian Conservative leaving ballet?

indicators.note: what leaves goes away, so that letter is removed

blocks.note: C is the abbreviation for Conservative
ballet is a form of dance, hence the question mark

explanation.surface: A Nordic Tory walks out of a ballet performance.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark admits ballet is only one example of the wider word.
explanation.definitionFit: A Dane is a person from Denmark, one of the Nordic nations.

clue.text: Surprise boy touring new fantasy world

indicators.note: to tour a place is to go all round it, so one piece surrounds another

blocks.note: wonder is amazement, surprise
a lad is a boy
N is the abbreviation for new

explanation.surface: A child is amazed on a trip around a magical new land.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Surprise' could be a verb, but here it is the noun for amazement.
explanation.definitionFit: Wonderland is Lewis Carroll's dreamlike realm visited by Alice, hence any imaginary marvellous place.
